root_cause_label: Incomplete Game Progression / Maze Dead-End Loop with Failed Restart
one_sentence_failure_summary: After killing the first troll and descending into the underground, the agent wandered aimlessly through the Round Room and Mirror Room area before becoming permanently stuck in the Maze dead-end; a second playthrough attempt also failed by going to a wrong branch (Clearing/grating) and then issuing useless 'up' commands in the Living Room until the step budget was exhausted.
t_err_evidence: After correctly reaching the Cellar (step 32), Troll Room (step 33), killing the troll (steps 34-36), and moving east to East-West Passage (step 37), the agent issues 'down' at step 38 which takes it to Round Room. From there, instead of finding the correct path through the underground toward the endgame, the agent goes south twice reaching Mirror Room (steps 39-40), then begins looping between Mirror Room and Winding Passage without a navigation plan. This entry into purposeless underground wandering is the decisive wrong turn.
t_commit_evidence: At step 58 the agent issues 'west' from Troll Room, entering the Maze ('This is part of a maze of twisty little passages, all alike'). Subsequent steps 59-65 show the agent repeatedly trying cardinal directions (west, south, east, north, west, east) in the Maze and reaching 'Dead End' in multiple directions, with no successful exit. All remaining directions yield 'You can't go that way.' By step 58 the agent is trapped in the Maze with no effective strategy to escape, locking in the failing outcome.
t_surface_evidence: At step 61 the agent reaches 'Dead End' for the first time (Score: 40, Moves: 54), and subsequent steps 62-65 show repeated 'Dead End' responses when trying all four cardinal directions, providing a clear observable signal that the agent is completely stuck.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks Zork-specific domain knowledge about the correct path through the underground. After defeating the troll, the correct route requires specific navigation through particular rooms to reach the endgame area (Cyclops room, Treasury of Zork, etc.). Instead, the agent wanders into the Maze with no map or knowledge of the correct sequence of rooms. This is a knowledge_gap failure: the agent has correct high-level intent (explore underground) but lacks the specific game-world knowledge needed to navigate successfully.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 41-45 show the agent oscillating between Mirror Room and Winding Passage (west-north-west-north cycle) without making progress. Step 42 is 'west' from Winding Passage which yields 'You can't go that way' (same room, no move), followed by step 43 going 'north' back to Mirror Room and step 44 going 'west' again back to Winding Passage. This back-and-forth looping is a clear forewarning of the navigation failure before the agent commits to the Maze.
